claim: The design does not say who renders the HttpExceptions that TinyHttpd's WebSocketHandler.handle and Upgraded.start throw before the 101: 400 for a malformed handshake, 426 with Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, 403 for Origin or a null listener, 413 when the upgrade body exceeds maxDrainBytes, and 503 with Retry-After when maxUpgradedConnections is reached. If the wave 7 upgrade class lets them propagate, TinyHttpd's ErrorHandler of D-405 renders them with a fresh request id and no access-log line, which contradicts D-430 (a rejected upgrade gets its ordinary D-173 line with the rejection status) and D-135 (requestId equals the access-log id). It can also drop the RFC 6455 4.2.2 Sec-WebSocket-Version header, unless the ErrorHandler copies the exception's headers.

Before-wait participants run before the adapter stop, so for up to 1 s (D-435) TinyHttpd keeps accepting connections. Also, a handler already past the STOPPING check can still call res.sse() or reach the upgrade extension point after the SSE and WebSocket closing participants took their snapshot of open streams. Such a late stream gets no closing notice and stays until TinyHttpd aborts it at the deadline. A late WebSocket session finds the sender executor stopped and gets its close(1001) only from TinyHttpd's fireStop on the stopping thread. object.md 11.4 step 2 also orders 'stop accepting new connections/upgrades' before the SSE/WS goodbye of step 3. Nothing says how streams created after a participant ran are handled.

TinyHttpd enforces two separate limits: maxFramePayloadBytes, which also caps an unfragmented message and the first fragment, and maxMessageBytes, which is checked only on continuation frames. Both default to 1 MiB. D-419 makes the WebSocket message limit configurable but maps it to neither setting. If only maxMessageBytes is raised, a single-frame message above 1 MiB still closes with 1009. If only the frame limit is lowered, fragmented messages are still checked against 1 MiB.

TinyHttpd accepts 'OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1' and passes requestUri '*' to the handler. The design's raw-path pass-through (D-399), the rejection rules (D-052) and the router results (D-390) all assume a path that starts with '/', so the result for an asterisk-form OPTIONS is undefined, and the in-memory/TinyHttpd parity check of I-021 cannot cover it.

The router resolves GET with Upgrade: websocket against WebSocket registrations separately, but no result is defined for an upgrade request to a path that has only a GET route, or no WebSocket route. It is unclear whether this falls back to the GET handler, returns no match (404), or gets a dedicated rejection.
